run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: Only one of the four available data sources worked in this Run: the Elasticsearch index app-262-prod-logs. Prometheus, Jaeger and Kubernetes (cluster production) all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags, kubernetes_jq_query, kubernetes_count, kubernetes_tabular_query), so no pod status, restarts, config-change or fault-injection settings, error rates, latencies or traces could be checked. The index holds only 5 documents in the authorized window, and the cluster field confirms the errors belong to cluster production-us-east-1 (US prod): checkout-service logged 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)' at 2026-11-20T19:57:12Z, payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 2026-11-20T20:57:12Z, and checkout-service logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)' at 2026-11-20T21:27:12Z, the newest sample in the window. The only samples from cluster production-eu-west-1 are checkout-service INFO lines ('Healthy: success rate 99.7%' at 21:27:12Z, 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' at 20:57:12Z), i.e. a different cluster and not evidence about US-east health. The best-supported reading is a hypothesis: payment-service's outbound calls to the external provider stripe-us (/v1/charges) exceeding 30s, with checkout-service then opening a circuit breaker toward payment-service. The provider itself is outside the observable cluster and could not be verified, and nothing available rules out an in-cluster cause inside payment-service (latency/fault injection, pod-level problem), so no root-cause object is named.

claims.text: The index app-262-prod-logs contains exactly 5 log documents inside 2026-11-19T21:57:21Z–2026-11-20T21:57:21Z: 3 from cluster production-us-east-1 and 2 from cluster production-eu-west-1; by service, 4 are checkout-service and 1 is payment-service; by level, 3 are ERROR and 2 are INFO.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-20T19:57:12Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service payment-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-20T20:57:12Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, service checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-20T21:27:12Z, the newest sample in the window: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)'.

The only documents from cluster production-eu-west-1 are checkout-service INFO lines 'Healthy: success rate 99.7%' at 2026-11-20T21:27:12Z and 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' at 2026-11-20T20:57:12Z; they belong to a different cluster and say nothing about the health of production-us-east-1 services.

Most likely deepest visible cause: the external payment provider referenced as stripe-us / Stripe-US did not answer payment-service's /v1/charges calls within 30s, payment-service surfaced upstream timeouts, and checkout-service consequently opened a circuit breaker toward payment-service (failure rate 44%). This is inferred from log text only; the provider is outside the cluster and no metric, trace or Kubernetes evidence confirms it.

Alternative candidate not excluded: an in-cluster fault inside payment-service itself (for example its own latency/timeout configuration, fault-injection setting or a pod-level problem) produced the 30s timeouts; this could not be checked because the Kubernetes and Prometheus sources were unavailable.

Rejected as the origin of the observed errors: cluster production-eu-west-1. Both of its samples in the window are INFO 'Healthy' lines for checkout-service, and none of the three ERROR documents carries that cluster value.

When Prometheus is reachable, confirm the payment path with rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count/rpc_grpc_status_code for service_name=payment and rpc_service pointing at the Stripe channel, plus traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment",status_code="ERROR"} and checkout's own error rate, before attributing the cause to the external provider.

When Kubernetes is reachable, inspect the payment-service and checkout-service deployments, their ReplicaSets/pods (restart counts, last termination reason, events) and any ConfigMaps carrying timeout, latency or failure-injection settings for those services, to decide between the external-provider hypothesis and an in-cluster configuration fault.

gaps: Kubernetes cluster production could not be read at all in this Run: kubernetes_jq_query (events grouped by involvedObject.kind/namespace/reason, pods, namespaces), kubernetes_count (pods, deployments) and kubernetes_tabular_query (deployments, events in namespace production) each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so pod status, restart counts, last termination reasons, ReplicaSet/ownership changes and ConfigMap fault-injection settings are unknown.

Prometheus could not be queried: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or status-code series (for example traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_grpc_status_code) were observed for payment-service, checkout-service or any other service.

Jaeger could not be queried: traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no spans, parent-child call edges or error spans exist in this evidence; the checkout→payment→stripe-us call path is inferred from log text only.
The external provider written as stripe-us / Stripe-US is outside the cluster and no source could observe it; whether it was slow, erroring or unreachable is unverified.

The index app-262-prod-logs has only 5 documents in the whole 24h window (none between 2026-11-19T21:57:21Z and 2026-11-20T19:57:12Z), so baseline behaviour before the 19:57:12Z first error is unknown rather than known-healthy, and any earlier onset of the incident cannot be timed.

It is unknown whether checkout-service or payment-service pods restarted, were redeployed or had configuration changed during the window; no Kubernetes or change-history source was available (the change_history integration is not integrated in this Run).
next_steps: Query Prometheus for payment-service and checkout-service error-rate and latency series over the window to establish a pre-19:57Z baseline and confirm the failure-rate figure (44%) cited in the circuit-breaker log line.
Read payment-service pod logs and events, including previous-container logs, and check deployment/ReplicaSet history for restarts or config-only rollouts during 19:57Z–21:27Z.
Review ConfigMaps for payment-service and checkout-service for any latency, timeout or failure-injection settings and whether they were switched on during the window.
